Synchronous bridge Ok means task dispatch, not sync completion. Constructor retains borrowed listener in RefPtr; unsafe accessor clones it and stays behind an intentional private supertrait/private_bounds exception. This documents lifetime ownership and a local visibility choice, not Send/thread safety or proof every C++ implementation honors reference contracts.",

Header population is fallible before those persistence callbacks; state token changes only after processing each batch and can itself fail. Success callback result is explicitly discarded in original sync/folder completion, whereas current DoOperation warns if success callback returns error. Operation result and listener error remain distinct; logging is not rollback.",
        "Owned Stale wrapper takes an existing RefPtr as readily as a new header. It writes Message-ID (UUID fallback), optional attachment/read/date/author/replyTo/recipient/subject/priority/reference fields and size in order, stopping on native error with no rollback. Oversize size logs and skips that write yet can return Updated. Thus state means completed adapter update, not all fields present, complete native initialization, successful DB persistence or immutable object. Consuming conversion transfers RefPtr and borrowed conversion clones it. Current header utility adds later fields and current EWS sync passes IHeaderBlock instead of calling this utility; no later-entry credit.",
        "Common SafeListener default failure converts error and queries optional fallible interface. If absent it returns Ok without a terminal native failure callback; if present callback failure propagates to handle_error for logging. Historical concrete EwsMessageSyncListener declares fallible interface and delegates callbacks, but the generic trait does not require every arbitrary wrapper type to supply it.
